title: Leading Eureka and working with John Casimir's bands
summary: Howard's stretch leading the Eureka, the shared personnel of Eureka and Tuxedo bands, and later work with John Casimir.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: That was a long time ago. Oh yeah. How long were you leading the Eureka?

Well I don't know the exact number of years, but I stood with him off and on. I led a long time and then I went with Eddie. I played with anyone, any one of them that needed a trumpet playing or something like that, you know? Because at that time I never did work. Most of the folks would work well, I'd be right out of church. And they called me.
You never did work days? No. I see. No I never did. What about other brass bands in late years that you played with? What about some of them?

Well it was practically the same fellas, but different bands, just like the Eureka, like I told before, just like the Eureka and the Tuxedo band. They used practically the same bands, it'd be a different name.
John Kazma's band, the Eureka band right today. They worked together. John got a job, he's got this bass player, and then Eureka got something, they got this and so forth.
Yeah, they're both using Timber now.
Yeah, they're both using Timber. And Mother's Day she'd keep working with John. So that's the way they worked. Well that's the way it was going in them days.
Did you work steady with John ever? Yeah, I played a long time with John. When was that?
Oh, before I'd taken sick, I used to play with him.
Well, I, actually this time I was in the hospital.
And you were working with John pretty steady then?
Sometime when I wanted to, but I'd mostly give that walking up a little bit there.
